signature: Numerators added together and denominators added together, so 1/4 + 2/3 is written as 3/7.
plainName: Treating a fraction as two separate numbers when adding
repairQuestion: If you add half a pizza to half a pizza, how much pizza is there? Now look at what the rule you used gives for 1/2 + 1/2.
visualSvg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif">
<text x="0" y="14" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">1/2 + 1/2 should be one whole.</text>
<rect x="0" y="26" width="70" height="26" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<rect x="70" y="26" width="70" height="26" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<text x="146" y="44" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">= 1</text>
<text x="0" y="82" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Adding the bottoms gives 2/4, which is less.</text>
<rect x="0" y="94" width="140" height="26" fill="#F5F1E8" stroke="#14201E"/>
<rect x="0" y="94" width="70" height="26" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<line x1="35" y1="94" x2="35" y2="120" stroke="#14201E"/>
<line x1="105" y1="94" x2="105" y2="120" stroke="#14201E"/>
<text x="146" y="112" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">= 1/2</text>
<text x="0" y="142" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">The answer got smaller than what went in.</text>
</svg>

signature: A decimal with more digits after the point is chosen as the larger one, so 0.45 is said to be bigger than 0.5.
plainName: Reading a longer decimal as a bigger number
repairQuestion: Shade 0.5 and 0.45 on two hundred grids. Which one has more shaded in?

signature: An answer smaller than the starting number is rejected or corrected after multiplying, because multiplying is expected to increase it.
plainName: Expecting multiplying to always make a number bigger
repairQuestion: What is half of 10? Now write that as 10 x 1/2. Did multiplying make it bigger?

signature: An answer larger than the starting number is rejected after dividing, or the divisor and dividend are swapped to force a smaller answer.
plainName: Expecting dividing to always make a number smaller
repairQuestion: How many halves are there in 3 whole pizzas? Write that as a division and see what you get.

signature: The equals sign is read as an instruction to write an answer, producing running chains like 3 + 4 = 7 + 2 = 9.
plainName: Reading the equals sign as do something rather than is the same as
repairQuestion: Cover up both sides of your equals sign and read each one out loud. Are those two amounts the same?

signature: In a column subtraction the smaller digit is taken from the larger one regardless of which is on top, so 43 minus 27 gives 24.
plainName: Always subtracting the smaller digit from the larger one in a column
repairQuestion: Estimate first. Is 43 take away 27 closer to 20 or closer to 10? Now check your answer against that.

signature: Regrouping stalls at a zero digit, so the zero is skipped or left unchanged, as in 300 minus 124 giving 276 or 184.
plainName: Getting stuck when there is a zero to borrow across
repairQuestion: What is 300 written as tens? Show me 300 as 30 tens, then take one of those tens apart.

signature: Decimals are lined up at the right-hand edge like whole numbers instead of at the decimal point, so 3.5 + 0.25 gives 0.60 or 3.75 gives way to a misaligned sum.
plainName: Lining decimals up at the end instead of at the point
repairQuestion: Which column is the tenths column in each number? Put your finger on both and see if they line up.

signature: Fractions are ordered by the size of the denominator, so 1/5 is said to be bigger than 1/3.
plainName: Reading a bigger bottom number as a bigger fraction
repairQuestion: Would you rather have one slice of a cake cut into 3, or one slice of the same cake cut into 5?
visualSvg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif">
<text x="0" y="14" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">One whole, cut two ways.</text>
<rect x="0" y="24" width="240" height="28" fill="#F5F1E8" stroke="#14201E"/>
<rect x="0" y="24" width="80" height="28" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<line x1="160" y1="24" x2="160" y2="52" stroke="#14201E"/>
<text x="250" y="43" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">1/3</text>
<rect x="0" y="66" width="240" height="28" fill="#F5F1E8" stroke="#14201E"/>
<rect x="0" y="66" width="48" height="28" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<g stroke="#14201E">
<line x1="96" y1="66" x2="96" y2="94"/><line x1="144" y1="66" x2="144" y2="94"/><line x1="192" y1="66" x2="192" y2="94"/>
</g>
<text x="250" y="85" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">1/5</text>
<text x="0" y="122" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Five is the bigger number, but 1/5 is the</text>
<text x="0" y="140" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">smaller piece. More cuts, smaller pieces.</text>
</svg>

signature: A fraction is read and manipulated as two independent whole numbers stacked up, rather than as one quantity.
plainName: Treating a fraction as two separate numbers rather than one amount
repairQuestion: Where would 3/4 sit on a line from 0 to 1? Point to it.

signature: The perimeter formula is used where area is asked for, or the two answers are swapped, and units are given as plain units where squares are needed.
plainName: Mixing up the distance round the edge with the space inside
repairQuestion: Run your finger round the outside of the shape. Now put your hand flat on the middle of it. Which of those two did the question ask about?
visualSvg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif">
<text x="0" y="14" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Perimeter is the walk round the edge.</text>
<rect x="0" y="24" width="120" height="80" fill="#F5F1E8" stroke="#00A878" stroke-width="4"/>
<text x="0" y="126" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">4 + 6 + 4 + 6 = 20 units</text>
<text x="170" y="14" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Area is the squares inside.</text>
<rect x="170" y="24" width="120" height="80" fill="#00A878" stroke="#14201E"/>
<g stroke="#F5F1E8">
<line x1="190" y1="24" x2="190" y2="104"/><line x1="210" y1="24" x2="210" y2="104"/>
<line x1="230" y1="24" x2="230" y2="104"/><line x1="250" y1="24" x2="250" y2="104"/>
<line x1="270" y1="24" x2="270" y2="104"/>
<line x1="170" y1="44" x2="290" y2="44"/><line x1="170" y1="64" x2="290" y2="64"/><line x1="170" y1="84" x2="290" y2="84"/>
</g>
<text x="170" y="126" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">24 squares</text>
<text x="0" y="146" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Same rectangle, two different questions.</text>
</svg>

signature: An angle with longer drawn arms is judged to be the larger angle, even when the turn between the arms is the same or smaller.
plainName: Judging an angle by how long its lines are drawn
repairQuestion: If I rub out the ends of both lines so they are the same length, has the corner changed at all?
visualSvg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif">
<g stroke="#14201E" stroke-width="2" fill="none">
<path d="M 20 110 L 120 110"/>
<path d="M 20 110 L 91 39"/>
<path d="M 190 110 L 230 110"/>
<path d="M 190 110 L 218 82"/>
</g>
<path d="M 50 110 A 30 30 0 0 0 41 89" stroke="#00A878" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/>
<path d="M 220 110 A 30 30 0 0 0 211 89" stroke="#00A878" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/>
<text x="56" y="86" font-size="13" fill="#00A878">45</text>
<text x="226" y="86" font-size="13" fill="#00A878">45</text>
<text x="0" y="134" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">Longer arms, same turn. The angle is the</text>
<text x="0" y="150" font-size="13" fill="#14201E">amount of turn, not the length of the lines.</text>
</svg>

signature: A ratio is scaled by adding the same amount to both parts rather than multiplying, so 2:3 is scaled to 4:5 instead of 4:6.
plainName: Scaling a ratio by adding instead of by multiplying
repairQuestion: If the recipe is 2 cups to 3 cups and you double everything, how much of each do you use?

signature: Two successive percentage changes are added together, so 20 percent off then a further 10 percent off is treated as 30 percent off.
plainName: Adding two discounts together instead of applying them one after the other
repairQuestion: Work out the price after the first discount and write it down. Now what is the second discount taken off, the old price or that new one?

signature: Negative numbers are ordered by the size of the digits, so minus 8 is said to be greater than minus 3.
plainName: Ordering negative numbers by their digits instead of their position
repairQuestion: Which is colder, minus 8 degrees or minus 3 degrees? Now put both on a number line and see which is further left.

signature: The expression is evaluated strictly left to right, so 2 + 3 x 4 gives 20.
plainName: Working left to right instead of doing the multiplying first
repairQuestion: Read the line out loud with the multiplication as a single chunk. What is the 3 x 4 worth before you add anything?

signature: A letter is treated as an abbreviation for an object rather than a number, so 3a is read as three apples and a plus b is read as a fruit salad.
plainName: Reading a letter as a label for a thing rather than a number
repairQuestion: Finish this sentence out loud: the letter a stands for the number of what?

signature: An operation is chosen from a keyword rather than the situation, so altogether always triggers addition and left always triggers subtraction.
plainName: Picking the operation from a keyword instead of the story
repairQuestion: Tell me the story in your own words without using any numbers. What is actually happening?

signature: Rounding is applied one digit at a time from the right, so 4.649 rounds to 4.65 and then to 4.7 when one decimal place was asked for.
plainName: Rounding one digit at a time instead of looking at the whole number
repairQuestion: Which two tenths does 4.649 sit between? Which of those two is it closer to?

signature: The product of two decimals is expected to be longer or larger than both, so a shorter answer is treated as an error.
plainName: Expecting multiplying decimals to make a longer number
repairQuestion: What is 0.5 of 0.5? Say it as half of a half and see how big that is.
